account: VoteMate announced the nationwide launch of its free AI ballot assistant on 16 October 2025. Its original release described conversational, multilingual access to candidate and ballot-measure information. The release reported that the soft launch had reached thousands of voters in 30 states. The undated AI Opportunity Inventory submission reports 7,652 beta users and acknowledges the absence of measured effects on voters. That usage count is not a benefit estimate. In May 2026, Ballotpedia confirmed an agreement for direct integration of its election data. VoteMate’s October 2026 transparency page describes several model providers, human review of AI-written candidate profiles, and connections to official and civic data sources. On 13 October 2026 VoteMate announced a connector to USAFacts government data. On 22 October 2026 NBC News reported that tens of thousands of voters had used VoteMate before the midterm elections and that its use was growing fast. These publications establish the service and its intended accessibility benefits. None of them measures a change in voter knowledge, accuracy, participation, or turnout. No source reports whether the answers were accurate.

ai_role.statement: Language models organize election information and answer questions using retrieved sources. A voter-benefit comparison has not been established. The October 2026 provider list does not establish the model used throughout the 2025 beta.
